title: Company kickoff playbook and risk register v0.1
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight playbook to prepare the company-wide kickoff (quarterly start), assemble the initial OKR draft for exec review, and maintain a first-pass risk register for the quarter. Intended audience: execs, leads, and the ops team running communications and the all-hands. Status: v0.1 — working draft for leadership input.

Scope and constraints:
- One-week sprint to lock in exec asks, finalize all-hands agenda, and publish the public-facing kickoff note.
- Focus areas: Hosted API reliability, Dedicated capacity launch readiness, Private deployment security checklist, Console rollout metrics, and Optimize cost controls.
- Assume product roadmaps are feature-frozen for the sprint except for critical bugfixes.

High-level timeline (key milestones):
- Day 0 (T minus 7): Draft OKRs + risk register circulated to execs.
- Day 2: Exec feedback due (48 hours). Consolidate and produce final OKR candidate list.
- Day 4: All-hands slide deck draft complete; rehearsal scheduled.
- Day 6: Publish kickoff email + internal Q&A doc; finalize run-of-show.
- Day 7 (Kickoff): All-hands, leadership AMA, team breakout sessions.

Proposed company OKR candidates (first-pass, to be refined):
- Objective 1: Deliver predictable, low-latency hosted inference for 95th percentile requests across top-10 customers.
  - KR1.1: Reduce 95p latency by 15% on hosted-api for models used in production (baseline: Jan 2026).
  - KR1.2: Decrease token cost per 1M tokens by 12% via batching and cache improvements.
  - KR1.3: Document and ship three model-specific kernel optimizations to CI that improve throughput.

- Objective 2: Make Dedicated and Private -> production-ready for enterprise pilots.
  - KR2.1: Deliver pilot onboarding flow for Dedicated with SLA docs and 99.9% availability target in staging.
  - KR2.2: Complete private deployment packaging and KMS integration for two regulated customers.
  - KR2.3: Reduce private deployment setup time to under 5 business days for standard network templates.

- Objective 3: Developer experience and observability that scales teams.
  - KR3.1: Launch per-route cost/latency breakdown in Console for top 5 customers by usage.
  - KR3.2: Increase automated regression detection coverage for prompts by 40% (eval harness expansion).
  - KR3.3: Publish 10 quickstarts for common integration patterns (webhooks, function calls, streaming).

Notes on framing for exec update: keep the narrative focused on economics + reliability + expandability. Example one-liner: "This quarter we harden inference economics (cost/latency), finish enterprise-ready packaging, and expand the console to give teams actionable cost controls."

All-hands (kickoff) proposed run-of-show (90 minutes):
- 0-5min: Welcome + housekeeping (People Ops).
- 5-20min: State of the company (CEO): topline growth, usage metrics, major wins.
- 20-35min: Product & Roadmap (Head of Product): where we are and what we’ll ship.
- 35-50min: Reliability & SLOs (SRE lead): what we fixed and what keeps us awake.
- 50-65min: Customer stories + Sales highlights (GTM).
- 65-80min: Demonstration: Console per-route insights + Dedicated onboarding flow (Demo team).
- 80-90min: Live AMA (moderated) + closing.

Communications plan (internal -> external):
- Internal: publish kickoff note, OKR summary, and FAQ doc in Confluence and #all-company Slack.
- External: short blog post (product highlights) + customer newsletter focusing on Dedicated/Private readiness and cost improvements (only after exec sign-off).

Risk register (initial):
- Risk A: Hosted capacity pressure during targeted performance optimizations.
  - Impact: customer-visible latency/regressions; potential crediting costs.
  - Likelihood: medium. Mitigation: staged rollout, synthetic traffic tests, canary metrics, rollback playbook (runbook id: PLAT-1423). Owner: SRE (Ravi).

- Risk B: Dedicated pilot delays due to packaging/network integration complexity.
  - Impact: delayed revenue recognition and customer churn.
  - Likelihood: medium-high. Mitigation: pre-provision templates, dedicated success engineer for each pilot, escalate blockers weekly. Owner: Solutions Engineering (Leila).

- Risk C: Console rollout introduces data privacy edge cases for Private customers.
  - Impact: compliance exposure and slowed enterprise adoption.
  - Likelihood: low-medium. Mitigation: gated feature flags, security review, KMS/HSM integration checklist. Owner: Security (Hannah).

- Risk D: Eval/regression detection misses production prompt drift.
  - Impact: model regressions affecting customer experience.
  - Likelihood: medium. Mitigation: expand eval coverage, integrate feedback loop from CS, weekly alerting. Owner: Applied ML (Marcus).

Operational asks (pre-kickoff to-dos):
- Slides: Product + SRE + GTM to submit deck sections by Day 3. (Owners: Product, SRE, GTM)
- Rehearsal: schedule two rehearsals — exec run-through & moderator prep. (Owner: People Ops)
- FAQ: draft internal FAQ with known questions and link to Jira runbook. (Owner: Comms/People Ops)
- Tech checks: demo environment and recording permissions validated two days prior. (Owner: Infra)
- Survey: short pre-kickoff pulse survey to collect top-3 questions from employees. (Owner: People Ops)

Metrics to show during the opening slides (suggested):
- 90-day active customers (trend), requests per second served, 95p latency trend (hosted), month-over-month cost per 1M tokens, Dedicated signups in pipeline, number of private deployments under NDA.

Open questions / items for exec input:
- Which metric is the single north-star for the quarter? (options: cost per token, 95p latency, Dedicated revenue).
- How aggressive should the rollout cadence be for kernel optimizations vs. risk of short-term regressions?
- Which customer stories should be highlighted in the kickoff to maximize GTM impact?

Appendix: quick references and templates
- Slide template: confluence:COMPANY-KICKOFF-2026/slides-template
- Runbook for rollback and canary checks: JIRA:PLAT-1423
- Dedicated pilot checklist: confluence:DEDICATED/PILOT-CHECKLIST

Quick wins / short list (for first 30 days):
- Ship Console per-route cost view MVP for top routes.
- Run a focused synthetic load test on hosted API against top models.
- Prep two enterprise pilot kits (network template + onboarding doc).

Unresolved / parking lot items (for next iteration):
- Hiring asks related to SRE on-call coverage — fill priority for Q2.
- Cross-team cost allocation model decision: central chargeback vs. route-level showback.

Bottom line (one-liner): This kickoff should set expectations: we will prioritize production economics (latency & cost) while finishing enterprise readiness for Dedicated and Private deployments. The playbook above gives the ops checklist and risk map — please comment inline with edits before Day 2 so we can incorporate into the exec packet.

TODO (owners and due dates):
- [ ] Product deck section submit (Owner: Marcus) — due 2026-02-12
- [ ] SRE runbook final review (Owner: Ravi) — due 2026-02-13
- [ ] Comms kickoff note draft (Owner: Leila) — due 2026-02-14
- [ ] People Ops rehearsal scheduling (Owner: Hannah) — due 2026-02-15

Notes to self: keep the kickoff short and operational — avoid long roadmap deep dives in the all-hands; use breakout sessions for detailed cross-functional planning.

End of v0.1. Please add comments directly in Drive and tag @aisha for urgent items.
